textToPptPptGuide.subtitle: Start a presentation in PowerPoint (.pptx) from a text outline with titles, bullets and tables. Pick a look, then finish it in PowerPoint. No PowerPoint needed.
faq: Is the Text to PowerPoint Maker free?
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up, no watermark and no limit on how many files you make. The file is made on your own device.
What starting points does the Text to PowerPoint Maker have?
It has starters for a short talk, a how-to or a report with a table. Each fills the outline with a full sample that you replace with your own words.
How do I write the slides?

Type them as text. A line that starts with # begins a new slide, and lines that start with a dash become bullet points. A line that starts with ## makes a section slide, > makes a big statement slide, == starts a column and a line of | cells | makes a table.
Can I change the colours, design and font?

Yes. Choose one of 12 designs, such as Navy and gold, Teal, Sunrise or Dark, and each one changes the colours, the title slide and the heading style. Then pick a font. The preview changes straight away.
Can I add pictures, charts or animations?
Not here. This tool makes text and table slides with a clean layout. Open the .pptx in PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office to add pictures, charts, animation and speaker notes.
Do I need PowerPoint to make this?

No. You do not need PowerPoint, or any app or account, to make it: this page builds the .pptx file in your browser, free. Later, when you want to change it, it opens in PowerPoint, Google Slides, WPS Office and LibreOffice Impress. Fonts and line breaks can look a little different from one app to another, so look through the slides once before you present.
Do I have to replace the text in square brackets?
Yes. Anything in [square brackets] is a prompt that tells you what to write. Replace it before you present. The page shows a reminder while any are left.
Is my presentation uploaded or saved on a server?
No. What you type and the PowerPoint file stay on your device, and {{siteName}} does not receive them. Nothing you type is saved, and Start again goes back to the original starter.

sections.heading: A clear start for a presentation
paragraphs: A presentation is usually made for anyone who needs slides fast. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for a short talk, a how-to or a report with a table, and you write the real content. Write one idea on each slide and keep each bullet short.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: What each starting point gives you
paragraphs: Short talk makes five slides: The problem, three main points and What to do next. It suits a talk of about five minutes, where each main point gets one slide and one spoken example.

How to makes seven slides: What you will learn, What you need, three numbered steps, Common mistakes and Summary. Replace Step 1, 2 and 3 with the real steps and add a line under each saying what the audience should see happen.

Report with a table makes four slides, and its Results slide holds a table with Item, Target and Actual columns, so type your figures as rows that start with a vertical bar. Compare options adds a Side by side table for cost, time and risk, and Story or lesson follows a start, a problem, a fix and a takeaway. Blank gives a single slide when you already know the shape you want.

sections.heading: Finish it in PowerPoint
paragraphs: The file has a title slide, one layout for each kind of slide and real slide titles, so the outline view in PowerPoint works.
Open it to add pictures, charts and animation, move slides around and add speaker notes. Replace every prompt in [square brackets] with your own words first.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so what you type is never uploaded. The file has no macros and no links to the internet.
The tool only lays out the words you give it. Check every name, date and figure before you present or share the slides.

sections.heading: A clear start for a pitch deck
paragraphs: A pitch deck is usually made for founders, small business owners and students. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for a startup pitch and a product launch, and you write the real content. Put one idea on each slide, and use your own real numbers.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: The slides in each pitch outline
paragraphs: Startup pitch has nine slides in the usual order investors expect: The problem, Our solution, How it works, Market, Business model, Traction, Competition, Team and The ask. Short investor pitch has eight: Problem, Solution, Product, Market, How we make money, Traction, Team and The ask.

Product launch is a five-slide deck for customers, not investors: The need, Meet your product, Why people will choose it, Plans and prices, and Launch plan. Service business has seven slides and adds Who we serve and What customers say, which suit a shop, clinic or agency that sells to local customers.

In every outline, put one claim on each slide and back it with a number you can defend, such as customers, orders or months of sales. The tool lays out your words but cannot check them, so remove any figure you cannot prove before you send the deck.

sections.heading: Finish it in PowerPoint
paragraphs: The file has a title slide, one layout for each kind of slide and real slide titles, so the outline view in PowerPoint works.
Open it to add pictures, charts and animation, move slides around and add speaker notes. Replace every prompt in [square brackets] with your own words first.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so what you type is never uploaded. The file has no macros and no links to the internet.
The tool only lays out the words you give it. Check every name, date and figure before you present or share the slides.

sections.heading: A clear start for a business proposal deck
paragraphs: A business proposal deck is usually made for freelancers, agencies and small businesses. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for a client proposal and a company profile, and you write the real content. Show the client need first, and then your offer and the cost.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: What goes on each proposal slide
paragraphs: Client proposal has seven slides: Who we are, What we understood, What we will do, Plan and timeline, Cost, Why choose us and Next steps. Write What we understood in the client's own words first, because it shows you listened before you sell.

Quote and scope also has seven, and includes a Not included slide. Listing what is left out is the quickest way to prevent an argument about extra work later. Company profile and Team introduction have five slides each and are meant to be sent ahead of a meeting.

This tool turns on an Agenda slide, which is built from your section titles when there are at least two, so it appears right after the title slide without extra typing. Prices and terms are your own; the tool does not know your rates or your legal terms, so read the Cost and Terms slides twice.

sections.heading: Finish it in PowerPoint
paragraphs: The file has a title slide, one layout for each kind of slide and real slide titles, so the outline view in PowerPoint works.
Open it to add pictures, charts and animation, move slides around and add speaker notes. Replace every prompt in [square brackets] with your own words first.

sections.heading: A clear start for a lesson presentation
paragraphs: A lesson presentation is usually made for teachers, tutors and trainers. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for a one-class lesson and a revision deck, and you write the real content. Keep each slide to one idea so the class can follow it.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: How the lesson outlines are planned
paragraphs: Lesson has seven slides that follow one class period: What we will learn today, Let us recall, a New idea, an Example, Try it yourself, Remember and Check your learning. The recall slide at the start lets students bring back yesterday's idea before the new one arrives.

Explain a concept has seven slides and starts with Think first, so students guess before you explain. It gives two examples before Try it. Revision has four slides: What to revise, Key words, Compare and Exam tips. Words and meanings has four, ending in a Quick check you can read aloud.

Keep each slide to one idea and three or four short lines. If a slide needs more, split it by adding another line that starts with a hash mark. You can change the design and font before you make the file, so try a plain light design if your classroom screen is hard to read.

sections.heading: A clear start for a status update deck
paragraphs: A status update deck is usually made for team leads, managers and freelancers. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for a weekly update and a monthly review, and you write the real content. Put the summary and the decisions you need up front.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: Choosing the right status outline
paragraphs: Weekly update has six slides: Summary, Done this week, Plan for next week, Milestones, Problems and help needed, and Decisions needed. Put the decision you need from the audience on the last slide so the meeting ends with an answer, not a discussion.

Monthly review has four slides and compares Results against plan, then What we learned. Monthly report has five and separates What went well from What did not, which keeps good news from hiding the problems. Launch readiness has five slides with a Checklist and Open risks, meant for the meeting before go-live.

Use a table slide for numbers, with the first row as the heading. Write the real dates and figures yourself; the tool only formats them. Use a table for Milestones with Due and Status columns, as the starter does, so late items are easy to spot.

paragraphs: A school project presentation is usually made for students, class presenters and college seminar speakers. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for a school project and a seminar, and you write the real content. Use short points and keep your own notes for what you will say.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: What each school starter covers
paragraphs: School project has seven slides: Introduction, Aim, What I did, What I found, Table of results, Conclusion and Thanks. Science project has six and begins with My question and What I thought would happen, so the result can be compared with the guess.

Seminar or talk has seven, from an Outline slide through Background, three parts, Conclusion and References. Famous person or place has six, including Quick facts, Important events and Sources. Write your sources on the last slide in your own words, since teachers check them.

Short sentences are better than copied paragraphs, and it is easier to speak from them. If your teacher gives a slide limit or a template, follow that; this tool gives a clear layout and does not know your school's rules.

sections.heading: Finish it in PowerPoint
paragraphs: The file has a title slide, one layout for each kind of slide and real slide titles, so the outline view in PowerPoint works.
Open it to add pictures, charts and animation, move slides around and add speaker notes. Replace every prompt in [square brackets] with your own words first.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so what you type is never uploaded. The file has no macros and no links to the internet.
The tool only lays out the words you give it. Check every name, date and figure before you present or share the slides.

sections.heading: A clear start for a quiz presentation
paragraphs: A quiz presentation is usually made for teachers, quiz hosts and event organisers. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for a general knowledge quiz and a class quiz, and you write the real content. Put the answers after each question for a live quiz, or at the end for a handout.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: How the quiz slides are built
paragraphs: Each question starts with Q:, then up to four options on their own lines starting A), B), C) and D), then an Answer: line. The General knowledge, Maths and Science starters each have four sample questions with the answer after each question, so you can see exactly how it looks before replacing them.

The Class quiz starter has three empty questions with answers collected at the end. When answers go at the end, the tool adds an Answers table slide after the last question, and splits it into more slides after nine answers. That is useful when you want to read all the questions first and reveal the marks together.

Write the answer as the option letter, such as B, or as the letter with its text. Check that the answer line matches the right option before you present; the tool copies what you type and cannot tell if a quiz key is wrong.

sections.heading: A clear start for an event programme deck
paragraphs: An event programme deck is usually made for schools, societies and organisers. Slides work best when each one has a single idea and only a few short lines.
This tool gives you the structure for an annual day and a workshop, and you write the real content. Show the programme table on one slide so everyone sees the same schedule.
You do not need PowerPoint to make it. The file is built in your browser, and you only need PowerPoint, Google Slides or WPS Office later if you want to keep editing it.

sections.heading: The slides in each event outline
paragraphs: Annual day or function has four slides: Programme, Our guests, Awards and prizes and Vote of thanks. Sports day has six: Welcome, Programme, Teams, Rules, Prizes and Thank you. Both suit a stage screen that is shown while the event runs.

Workshop or meeting has Welcome, Agenda, Ground rules and Close, and works for a training day or a society meeting. Family function has Welcome, The day, Where to find things and Thank you, which is handy for telling guests where food, parking and rooms are.

Put times in a table slide, with one row for each item, so the programme is easy to scan. Choose a high-contrast design such as Bold Black and Yellow or Midnight when the screen is far from the audience. Names, times and venues are yours to type, and you should read them aloud once before the event.
